## 📋 Policy 10000 — Code of Ethics and Related Matters

### 🎯 Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to establish standards of ethical conduct for all employees and ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.[1]

---

### 🌐 Scope
This policy applies to all full-time, part-time, and temporary employees of the organization.[1]

---

### ✅ Standards of Conduct
All employees are expected to conduct themselves with integrity, honesty, and professionalism in all business dealings. Employees must avoid conflicts of interest and disclose any potential conflicts to their supervisor or the Ethics Committee.[1]

---

### ⚖️ Conflicts of Interest
Employees must not engage in activities that conflict with the interests of the organization. This includes:
- Financial interests in competing businesses
- Accepting gifts from vendors exceeding **$25** in value
- Using company resources for personal gain[1]

---

### 📣 Reporting Violations
Employees who become aware of violations of this Code of Ethics are encouraged to report them through the **Ethics Hotline** or directly to the **Ethics Committee**. Reports may be made **anonymously**. The organization prohibits retaliation against employees who report violations in good faith.[1]

---

### 🔍 Compliance and Enforcement
Violations of this Code of Ethics may result in disciplinary action, **up to and including termination of employment**. The Ethics Committee is responsible for investigating reported violations and recommending appropriate corrective action.[1]

---

---

## 📋 Purpose & Scope

The purpose of this policy is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to **all regular full-time employees who have completed their probationary period**.[1]

---

## ⏱️ PTO Accrual

Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, on a per-pay-period basis:

| Years of Service | PTO Accrual |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days per year |
| 3–5 years | 20 days per year |
| 6–10 years | 25 days per year |
| 11+ years | 30 days per year |[1]

---

## 🗓️ PTO Usage

PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the designated time-off system. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

## 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance

Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual stops once the maximum balance is reached.[1]

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO, up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

---

## 📋 Scope & Eligibility

| | **Full-Time (Policy 50010)** | **Part-Time (Policy 50020)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Who it applies to** | All regular full-time employees | All regular part-time employees working **minimum 20 hrs/week** |
| **Requirement** | Must have completed probationary period | Must have completed probationary period |

The full-time policy applies to all regular full-time employees who have completed their probationary period.[1]The part-time policy applies to all regular part-time employees who work a minimum of 20 hours per week and have completed their probationary period.[2]

---

## ⏱️ PTO Accrual

### Full-Time Employees
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on years of service:
- **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
- **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
- **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
- **11+ years:** 30 days per year

PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.[1]

### Part-Time Employees
Part-time employees accrue PTO on a **pro-rated basis** calculated from their regularly scheduled hours. Accrual rates are:
- **0–2 years:** 0.0385 hours per hour worked
- **3–5 years:** 0.0577 hours per hour worked
- **6+ years:** 0.0769 hours per hour worked[2]

---

## 🗓️ PTO Usage

- **Full-Time:** PTO may be used for vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose. Employees must request PTO through the designated time-off system. Requests for three or more consecutive days require supervisor approval at least two weeks in advance.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees must request PTO in accordance with their regular schedule. PTO is deducted in **hourly increments**. Requests must be submitted through the time-off system.[2]

---

## 🔄 Carryover

| | **Full-Time** | **Part-Time** |
|---|---|---|
| **Carryover Limit** | Up to **40 hours** per year | Up to **20 hours** per year |
| **Maximum Balance** | 240 hours | Not specified (accrual stops at max) |

Full-time employees may carry over up to 40 hours of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The maximum PTO balance at any time is 240 hours, and accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1]Part-time employees may carry over up to 20 hours of unused PTO per calendar year, and accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[2]

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

- **Full-Time:** Employees who separate from employment in good standing will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

- **Part-Time:** The part-time policy does not specify a PTO payout upon separation.

---

## 🔁 Transitioning from Part-Time to Full-Time

Part-time employees who transition to full-time status will have their PTO balance **converted** and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy.[2]

---

## 📝 Key Takeaways

| Feature | Full-Time | Part-Time |
|---|---|---|
| Accrual Method | Days/year (service-based) | Hours per hour worked (pro-rated) |
| Carryover | 40 hours | 20 hours |
| Max Balance | 240 hours | Not specified |
| Separation Payout | Up to 80 hours | Not specified |
| Usage Tracking | Per request | Hourly increments |

The main distinction is that **full-time employees earn a fixed number of days per year** based on tenure, while **part-time employees earn PTO proportionally** based on actual hours worked.

## 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
This policy is designed to **provide income protection for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability**.[1]

### Eligibility (Scope)
This policy applies to **all regular full-time employees** who have completed **90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

### How to File a Claim
Employees must:
1. **Notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability.
2. Submit a **completed claim form and supporting medical documentation** to the disability administrator **within 15 days**.[1]

---

## 📋 Policy 10000 — Code of Ethics and Related Matters

### 🎯 Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to establish standards of ethical conduct for all employees and ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.[1]

---

This policy applies to all full-time, part-time, and temporary employees of the organization.[1]

---

All employees are expected to conduct themselves with integrity, honesty, and professionalism in all business dealings. Employees must avoid conflicts of interest and disclose any potential conflicts to their supervisor or the Ethics Committee.[1]

Employees must not engage in activities that conflict with the interests of the organization. This includes:

Here is a comprehensive overview of what the **Full-Time Paid Time Off (PTO) Policy (Policy 50010)** covers:

---

## 📋 Purpose & Scope

The purpose of Policy 50010 is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their **probationary period**.[1]

---

## ⏳ PTO Accrual

Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, on a **per-pay-period basis**, as follows:

| Years of Service | PTO Accrual |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days per year |
| 3–5 years | 20 days per year |
| 6–10 years | 25 days per year |
| 11+ years | 30 days per year |[1]

---

## 🗓️ PTO Usage

PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval **at least two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

## 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance

Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual **stops** when the maximum balance is reached.[1]

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO, up to a **maximum of 80 hours**, at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

- **11+ years:** 30 days per year

PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.[1]

---

## 📋 Policy 50020 — PTO for Part-Time Employees

**Scope:** This policy applies to all **regular part-time employees** who work a **minimum of 20 hours per week** and have completed their probationary period.[2]**PTO Accrual** is pro-rated based on hours worked:
- **0–2 years:** 0.0385 hours per hour worked

|---|---|

| Regular **part-time** (≥20 hrs/week, post-probation) | **Policy 50020** |

> **Note:** If you are a part-time employee who **transitions to full-time**, your PTO balance will be converted and you will begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy.[2]

Here is a detailed comparison of the **Full-Time PTO Policy (Policy 50010)** and the **Part-Time PTO Policy (Policy 50020)**:

---

## 📋 PTO Policy Comparison: Full-Time vs. Part-Time

### 1. 🎯 Purpose & Scope

| | **Full-Time (Policy 50010)** | **Part-Time (Policy 50020)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | To establish the PTO policy for eligible full-time employees.[1] | To establish the PTO policy for eligible part-time employees.[2] |
| **Scope** | Applies to all regular full-time employees who have completed their probationary period.[1] | Applies to all regular part-time employees who work a minimum of 20 hours per week and have completed their probationary period.[2] |

---

### 2. 📈 PTO Accrual

**Full-Time Employees** accrue PTO in **days per year**, based on years of service:



| Years of Service | PTO Accrual |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days/year |
| 3–5 years | 20 days/year |
| 6–10 years | 25 days/year |
| 11+ years | 30 days/year |

PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.[1]

**Part-Time Employees** accrue PTO on a **pro-rated, per-hour-worked** basis:



| Years of Service | Accrual Rate |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 0.0385 hours per hour worked |
| 3–5 years | 0.0577 hours per hour worked |
| 6+ years | 0.0769 hours per hour worked |

[2]

> **Key Difference:** Full-time employees have a fixed accrual in days/year, while part-time employees accrue proportionally based on actual hours worked.

---

### 3. 🗓️ Usage & Scheduling

- **Full-Time:** PTO may be used for vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose. Employees must request PTO through the designated time-off system. Requests for three or more consecutive days require supervisor approval at least two weeks in advance.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees must request PTO in accordance with their regular schedule. PTO is deducted in hourly increments. Requests must be submitted through the time-off system.[2]

> **Key Difference:** Full-time policy allows broad use (vacation, illness, personal) and specifies a 2-week advance notice for 3+ consecutive days. Part-time PTO is deducted in hourly increments and must align with the employee's regular schedule.

---

### 4. 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance

| | **Full-Time** | **Part-Time** |
|---|---|---|
| **Carryover Limit** | Up to 40 hours of unused PTO to the following calendar year.[1] | Up to 20 hours of unused PTO per calendar year.[2] |
| **Maximum Balance** | 240 hours maximum at any time.[1] | Not specified (accrual stops at max balance) |
| **Accrual Stop** | Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1] | Accrual stops when maximum balance is reached.[2] |

> **Key Difference:** Full-time employees can carry over twice as many hours (40 vs. 20) and have a defined maximum balance of 240 hours.

---

### 5. 💼 PTO at Separation

- **Full-Time:** Employees who separate from employment in good standing will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of 80 hours at their current rate of pay.[1]

- **Part-Time:** No payout upon separation is mentioned in the part-time policy.

---

### 6. 🔀 Transitioning from Part-Time to Full-Time

Part-time employees who transition to full-time status will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy.[2]

---

This policy is designed to provide income protection for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.[1]

This policy applies to all regular full-time employees who have completed **90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

Short-term disability benefits are payable for up to **26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches the maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

### 🩺 Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

### 📝 Claim Process
Employees must notify their supervisor and Human Resources within **three (3) business days** of the onset of disability. A completed claim form and supporting medical documentation must be submitted to the disability administrator within **15 days**.[1]

Here is a detailed side-by-side comparison of the **Full-Time PTO Policy (Policy 50010)** and the **Part-Time PTO Policy (Policy 50020)**:

---

## 📋 Scope & Eligibility

| | **Full-Time (Policy 50010)** | **Part-Time (Policy 50020)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Who it covers** | All regular full-time employees who have completed their probationary period.[1] | All regular part-time employees who work a minimum of 20 hours per week and have completed their probationary period.[2] |

---

## ⏱️ PTO Accrual

**Full-Time employees** accrue PTO as a set number of **days per year**, based on tenure:



| Years of Service | Days per Year |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days |
| 3–5 years | 20 days |
| 6–10 years | 25 days |
| 11+ years | 30 days |

PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.[1]

---

**Part-Time employees** accrue PTO on a **pro-rated, per-hour-worked basis**:



| Years of Service | Hours Accrued per Hour Worked |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 0.0385 hrs |
| 3–5 years | 0.0577 hrs |
| 6+ years | 0.0769 hrs |

[2]

> 📌 **Note:** Full-time accrual has **4 tenure tiers** (including 11+ years), while part-time accrual has only **3 tiers** (capping at 6+ years).

---

## 📅 PTO Usage

- **Full-Time:** PTO may be used for vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose. Employees must request PTO through the designated time-off system. Requests for three or more consecutive days require supervisor approval at least two weeks in advance.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees must request PTO in accordance with their regular schedule. PTO is deducted in hourly increments. Requests must be submitted through the time-off system.[2]

---

## 🔄 Carryover

| | **Full-Time** | **Part-Time** |
|---|---|---|
| **Carryover limit** | Up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year.[1] | Up to **20 hours** of unused PTO per calendar year.[2] |
| **Maximum balance** | **240 hours**. Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1] | Accrual stops when maximum balance is reached.[2] *(No specific maximum balance stated.)* |

---

## 🚪 PTO at Separation

- **Full-Time:** Employees who separate from employment in good standing will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

- **Part-Time:** *(Policy 50020 does not specify a PTO payout at separation.)*

---

## 🔁 Transitioning from Part-Time to Full-Time

Part-time employees who transition to full-time status will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy.[2]

---

## 🔑 Key Takeaways

| Feature | Full-Time | Part-Time |
|---|---|---|
| Accrual method | Days/year (flat) | Hours per hour worked (pro-rated) |
| Max carryover | 40 hours | 20 hours |
| Max balance cap | 240 hours | Not specified |
| Separation payout | Up to 80 hours | Not specified |
| Consecutive-day approval | ✅ Required (2 weeks notice) | Not specified |
| PTO deduction unit | Not specified | Hourly increments |

Both policies require completion of the probationary period and use of the company's time-off system for requests. The primary difference lies in how PTO is **accrued** and the **carryover limits**, reflecting the proportional nature of part-time employment.

---

## 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
This policy is designed **to provide income protection for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability**.[1]

---

### Eligibility (Scope)
This policy applies to **all regular full-time employees who have completed 90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

---

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

---

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

---

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

---

### Claim Process
Employees must:
1. **Notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability.
2. Submit a **completed claim form and supporting medical documentation** to the disability administrator **within 15 days**.[1]

---

The purpose of this policy is to establish standards of ethical conduct for all employees and ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.[1]

This policy applies to all full-time, part-time, and temporary employees of the organization.[1]

Here is a comprehensive overview of the full-time **Paid Time Off (PTO) Policy** (Policy 50010):

---

## 📋 Purpose & Scope

The purpose of Policy 50010 is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their **probationary period**.[1]

---

## ⏱️ PTO Accrual

Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**:
- **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
- **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
- **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
- **11+ years:** 30 days per year

PTO accrues on a **per-pay-period basis**.[1]

---

## 🗓️ PTO Usage

PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

## 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance

Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**. Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1]

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

## 📋 Scope & Purpose

The purpose of this policy is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their **probationary period**.[1]

---

## ⏱️ PTO Accrual

Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, on a per-pay-period basis:

| Years of Service | PTO Days Per Year |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days |
| 3–5 years | 20 days |
| 6–10 years | 25 days |
| 11+ years | 30 days |[1]

---

## 🗓️ PTO Usage

PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

## 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance

Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual stops once this maximum is reached.[1]

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO, up to a maximum of **80 hours**, at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

## 📋 PTO Policy Comparison: Full-Time vs. Part-Time

### 1. 🎯 Purpose & Scope

| | **Full-Time (Policy 50010)** | **Part-Time (Policy 50020)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | To establish the PTO policy for eligible full-time employees.[1] | To establish the PTO policy for eligible part-time employees.[2] |
| **Eligibility** | All regular full-time employees who have completed their probationary period.[1] | All regular part-time employees who work a minimum of 20 hours per week and have completed their probationary period.[2] |

---

### 2. ⏱️ PTO Accrual Rates

- **Full-Time Employees** accrue PTO in **days per year** based on years of service:

  
  - **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
  - **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
  - **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
  - **11+ years:** 30 days per year

  PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.
  [1]

- **Part-Time Employees** accrue PTO in **hours per hour worked** (pro-rated):

  
  - **0–2 years:** 0.0385 hours per hour worked
  - **3–5 years:** 0.0577 hours per hour worked
  - **6+ years:** 0.0769 hours per hour worked
  [2]

---

### 3. 📅 Usage & Scheduling

| | **Full-Time** | **Part-Time** |
|---|---|---|
| **Eligible Uses** | Vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose.[1] | Not specified — general scheduling applies. |
| **How Deducted** | Not specified by specific increment. | PTO is deducted in hourly increments.[2] |
| **Approval Process** | Requests for three or more consecutive days require supervisor approval at least two weeks in advance.[1] | Requests must be submitted through the time-off system.[2] |

---

### 4. 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance

| | **Full-Time** | **Part-Time** |
|---|---|---|
| **Carryover Limit** | Up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year.[1] | Up to **20 hours** of unused PTO per calendar year.[2] |
| **Maximum Balance** | **240 hours**. Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1] | Accrual stops when maximum balance is reached.[2] (No specific maximum stated beyond carryover.) |

---

### 5. 💰 PTO at Separation

| | **Full-Time** | **Part-Time** |
|---|---|---|
| **Payout** | Employees who separate from employment in good standing will be paid for unused accrued PTO, up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1] | No separation payout provision specified in Policy 50020. |

---

### 6. 🔁 Status Change

Part-time employees who transition to full-time status will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy.[2]

---

### 🔑 Key Takeaways

- **Full-time employees** receive a more generous and structured PTO accrual in **days/year**, higher carryover limits (40 hrs), a defined maximum balance (240 hrs), and a separation payout.
- **Part-time employees** accrue PTO **hourly and proportionally**, with a lower carryover cap (20 hrs) and no specified separation payout.

### 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

**Purpose**

This policy is designed to provide **income protection** for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.[1]

---

**Eligibility**

This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed **90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

---

**Benefit Amount**

Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

---

**Duration of Benefits**

Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches the maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

---

**Qualifying Conditions**

Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

---

**Claim Process**

Employees must **notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability. A completed claim form and supporting medical documentation must be submitted to the disability administrator **within 15 days**.[1]
